discovery: Growth of ultrapure hexagonal boron nitride crystals enabling high-quality van der Waals heterostructures

nominees.name: Takashi Taniguchi
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

nominees.name: Kenji Watanabe
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics / materials physics (two-dimensional materials)
motivation: Using high-pressure, high-temperature solvent growth, Taniguchi and Watanabe produced hexagonal boron nitride crystals of exceptional purity, and they shared them freely with the world. Encapsulating graphene and other 2D materials in their hBN gives atomically flat, charge-free, insulating substrates and gate dielectrics. This raised device quality by orders of magnitude and turned van der Waals heterostructures into a precise platform for quantum physics. Their crystals underlie the fractional quantum Hall effect and Hofstadter butterfly in graphene, magic-angle superconductivity and correlated states in moiré systems, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect, 2D magnetism and ferroelectricity, and much of modern 2D optoelectronics. Few contributions have made so much new physics experimentally accessible to so many laboratories. Their patient materials craftsmanship is the quiet foundation of an entire field, and it merits the Nobel Prize in Physics.
